Facultative Water Reabsorption
• Mainly occurs in the collecting duct  & partly in late DCT.
• Regulated by ADH 
• ADH promotes AQP2 insertion.
• Varies according to hydration status.
• Helps produce concentrated urine.

Obligatory Water Reabsorption
• Occurs regardless of ADH.
• Mainly occurs in the PCT.
• About 65% of filtered water is reabsorbed.
• AQP1 is the major water channel.
• Also occurs in the descending limb.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৩৫) Antidiuretic Hormone is primarily synthesized in the:
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Explanation

ADH
• Primarily synthesized in the supraoptic nucleus of the hypothalamus.
• Also synthesized in the paraventricular nucleus.
• Stored and released from the posterior pituitary.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৩৬) Which zone of the adrenal cortex primarily secretes aldosterone?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Explanation

- The zona glomerulosa primarily secretes aldosterone, the principal mineralocorticoid.

Adrenal cortex
• Zona glomerulosa -  Aldosterone (mineralocorticoid)
• Zona fasciculata  -  Cortisol, corticosterone (glucocorticoids)
• Zona reticularis  -  Androgens (DHEA, androstenedione)

Adrenal medulla - Catecholamines
• Adrenaline (epinephrine)
• Noradrenaline (norepinephrine)
• Small amounts of dopamine

Mnemonic :  GFR — Make Good Sex
• G → Glomerulosa → Mineralocorticoids
• F → Fasciculata → Glucocorticoids
• R → Reticularis → Sex hormones

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৩৭) Which of the following most strongly stimulates growth hormone secretion?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Explanation

Stimulators
• Deep sleep
• Hypoglycaemia
• Exercise
• Fasting
• Stress
• GHRH
• Ghrelin

Inhibitors
• Ageing
• Obesity
• Hyperglycaemia
• Increased free fatty acids
• Somatostatin

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৩৮) Which type of nephron is mainly responsible for concentrating urine?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Explanation

• Juxtamedullary nephrons: Located near the corticomedullary junction.
• Have long loops of Henle and vasa recta.
• Maintain the medullary osmotic gradient, essential for urine concentration.
• Cortical nephrons: Have short loops and mainly contribute to routine urine formation.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৩৯) Which of the following primarily mediates growth hormone–induced linear growth?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Explanation

• IGF-1 (somatomedin C) is the major mediator of GH-induced linear growth.
• It is produced mainly by the liver in response to GH.
• IGF-1 promotes chondrocyte proliferation and bone growth.
• IGF-2 has a greater role in fetal growth.
• GIP is an incretin that enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion.
• Insulin promotes anabolic processes but is not the major mediator of GH-induced linear growth.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৪০) Which hormone acts through intracellular receptors to regulate gene transcription?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Explanation

- Thyroid hormones enter cells and act through intracellular receptors, regulating gene activity and protein synthesis.
• This increases metabolic activity and produces the physiological effects of thyroid hormones.

Receptor Locations
- Cell membrane  
  • Protein and polypeptide hormones
  • Catecholamines

- Intracellular
  • Steroid hormones
  • Thyroid hormones
  • Vitamin D

Hormones Acting Through Gene Activation
• Thyroid hormones: T₃, T₄
• Steroid hormones:
• Cortisol
• Aldosterone
• Estrogen
• Progesterone
• Testosterone
• Vitamin D: Calcitriol
